name: Final Destination
text:
You search the Tatterdemalion's console and discover its itinerary. Over a year ago, the ship departed in search of a trans-Saturnian asteroid of extrasolar origin codenamed "Fragment". The crew eventually found the mysterious object and sent several survey and excavation teams for unknown purposes. The mission proceeded smoothly, until the Tatterdemalion suddenly lost contact with one of its survey teams deep within the subterranean caverns of Fragment. Despite the disappearance, the mission was apparently deemed a success, and the ship was set to return home. You vaguely recall stepping out of a shuttle, onto the rocky surface of a golden asteroid. The stars glittered bright and red. You must have been on one of the Tatterdemalion's survey teams.
Each investigator at your location adds 1 tally mark next to their "Memories". You may gain up to 3 resources. Add this card to the victory display. Victory 1.

name: Into the Archives
text:
Within the digital environment of the ship, you come across a vault containing petabytes of encrypted data. It appears that the Tatterdemalion's archives contain the brain scans and histories of hundreds of people from the 20th and 21st century. According to these records, you were institutionalized after attempting to sabotage a theatre play. You lived the rest of your life in isolation, warning to all of "Carcosa" and of the one named "Hastur". After your death, your brain was preserved by the institution and eventually scanned for scientific research. Despite feeling sorrow for your past life, you can finally let go of that reality. Even though it's not exactly the world you expected, you've been given a second chance at life, and aim to not repeat the same mistakes.

name: K2-PS187 Cybernetic Brains
text:
You finally uncover the direct access point to interface with the Tatterdemalion's main computer, K2-PS187. However, you quickly realize that disabling or rewiring it will not be as simple as you anticipated. K2-PS187 is not a true computer at all, and is actually a cybernetic organism. Deep within the mechanics of the ship’s bridge is the computer core, and within it are the disembodied brains of six young children. These brains are linked together to form a very powerful super-computer. The situation sickens you to the core. Who would do such a thing? Damning these minds to an eternity of calculating ship trajectories and processing algorithms. You feel guilty, knowing that you must have been part of this heinous crew.

name: Strange is the Night
text:
Donning the EVA suit, you leave the pressurized atmosphere of the ship to climb across the outside of the vessel. The Tatterdemalion appears much larger from the outside -- you barely see the access point on the other side. It will take quite some time to traverse the ship. As you glide forwards, a glint from above catches your eye. A yellow and green flare undulates in the canvas of space. It dances in the sky and entwines into a singular design -- rings of concentric semicircles lined with strange runes, and at the center is a pair of wavy lines. You have seen this symbol before -- during the presentation of The King in Yellow. However, this wasn't the one in the Ward Theatre, but an amateur performance in the cramped and industrial interior of the Tatterdemalion. After the strange lights fade away, you realize you completely let go of your tethers and were beginning to drift away. With a small thrust of your suit's reaction control system, you grab hold of the ship once more and hastily climb your way to the next airlock, with a much firmer grip.
Add 2 tally marks next to your "Memories". Add this card to the victory display. Victory 1.

name: Elbrus Station
flavor:
QUANTUM FIELD UNSTABLE.
EVACUATE ELBRUS STATION IMMEDIATELY.

The warning startles you awake. Despite the troubling descent, the lander has coasted into one of the craters with minimal damage. It appears most of the asteroid has already been evacuated -- but then who stayed behind to send you the warning during your descent?
back_text:
You finally find the lone scientist on the asteroid -- he introduces himself as Erwin Simmons, the lead quantum researcher at the facility. "They stole the stabilizing shards!" Those cultists!" He explains the recent happenings. "Without the shards, the whole asteroid quickly lost itself in uncertainty. Everyone else was evacuated, but I stayed behind to contain the anomaly."
If there are 3 or more tally marks under "Impending Doom" in your Campaign Log:
"Unfortunately, it's too late -- the maelstrom is affecting my reality. You need to leave this asteroid as soon as you can, lest you get trapped here too!" Before you can react, the physicist fades out of existence right in front of you.
Shuffle the encounter discard pile into the encounter deck. Shuffle Erwin Simmons (Fading) with the top 3[per_investigator] cards of the encounter deck. Then, distribute them into each investigator's threat area, face-down, as evenly as possible. Proceed to act 2a, Destabilization, and remove act 2a, Quantum Zeno from the game.
Otherwise:
Despite the situation, he believes the facility can still be saved if you are able to help him distribute the modified Q-Crystal shards across the asteroid.
Put the set aside Erwin Simmons (Quantum Physicist) story asset into play under any investigator's control. This story asset does not take up an ally slot for this scenario. Proceed to act 2a, Quantum Zeno, and remove act 2a, Destabilization from the game.

flavor: A small, slender, non-threatening humanoid with large eyes and a round, bald head guards the entrance of the facility. They do not speak -- only ogles you from afar.
back_text:
The Grey alien suddenly dissolves into an array of light -- you realize now that it was only a hologram. A large crustacean-like entity crawls out of the shadows from behind it. You remember these aliens, the Mi-Go, who will often use manufactured disguises when dealing with humans, to appear less threatening. Another hologram animates into life. It exhibits the shapes of several humans exchanging jars of brains for stacks of golden plates and other minerals. This must have been a recording of the cultists' "negotiations". With its fungoid arms, the alien gestures towards the strange facility, as if inviting you in.
Flip The Greys to its other side (transfer any damage tokens on it to its other side). Each investigator with 3 or fewer "Memories" takes 1 horror. Advance to agenda 2a and act 2a. Do not remove doom from play. Move all doom from agenda 1 to agenda 2a. Add 2 doom to agenda 2a for each tally mark under "Impending Doom" in your Campaign Log.

You thought you defeated the Boogeyman, but it appears that it had been hiding within your memories, waiting for the right time to strike. "You've got nowhere to hide now! AHA-HA!" flavor: A man in an elegant black suit awaits you in the halls behind the stage, his face covered by a pale mask. You instantly recognize the actor who played the role of the Stranger -- one of the characters from The King in Yellow. He turns and disappears through an open doorway, as if taunting you to follow.
back_text:
As you face off with the Stranger, you get the sense that he is grinning beneath his pale, faceless mask. "Where is Fragment?" you ask, but he does not respond. "Who are you?" He remains silent, but brings his gloved hand up and slowly removes his mask, revealing a mirror image of yourself. "Who are you?" the doppelgänger asks threateningly. You step back in shock -- and your other self steps back in accordance. You point towards it - and it responds in kind. The stranger appears to mimic your every move.
Put a copy of the set aside Your Other Self into play in each investigator's threat area. Check your Campaign Log. If you have uncovered the cultists' inhuman methods, each investigator may either (choose one): - Gain 1 clue from the token bank and heal up to 2 damage and 2 horror. - Add 1 tally mark next to their "Memories".

The other you falls down to the ground in defeat. You have finally vanquished your demons. The doppelgänger cries out in defiance. "You don't know what you are fighting. Within the palaces of Carcosa, after we freed the princess, we uncovered the true nature of Hastur, and it is greater than any one of us could have imagined... it is inevitable..." You watch as your other self disintegrates into ashen dust and dissipate into the air...
(→R2)

name: Arrival of the King
text:
Standing and sitting in small groups around the ballroom, are statues of the inhabitants of the Palace. They are all gaily dressed for a masquerade, though they have all unmasked. On closer inspection, you realize the statues are speaking in low, stunned tones, as if time here has slowed almost to a standstill. They share amongst each other the faintest rumors about the Royal Family of Carcosa. It is an echo of the moment the city of Yhtill -- wherein the Palace lay -- became Carcosa, and the royal family of the palace learned that they were inevitably doomed. They stand around now, morose and uncertain. The people of the Palace were truly lost in both mind and soul.

name: Delights
text:
Within the gardens are plants that bear no resemblance to anything natural of Earth. Fruits of unrecognizable chromatics populate the obsidian towers of web-like silk. The scene describes a fever dream of inconceivable shapes and smells that extends across the very limits of your mind. You pick up one of the fruits that fell onto the floor to examine it, only to watch it rot and decay through your fingers. Time in the realm of Carcosa does not behave as it does in your dimension. When you finally exit the forbidden gardens, an air of relief overcomes you. Although you cannot describe the nature of what you experienced, it was nonetheless truly invigorating and you feel like you are finally in control of your own destiny.
You may choose and remove any non - [auto_fail] symbol token from the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. Add this card to the victory display. Victory 1.

name: For You Alone
text:
The halls grow increasingly labyrinthine, the chambers, once brightly lit and spacious, grow dark and dusty and cramped. You further stray into the labyrinth until you reach a chamber with walls and columns covered in shelves. Each shelf has a glass bottle upon it, no two of which was alike in shape or design, and each bottle is inscribed with a name. There is an uncountable number of these flasks -- enough to account for every individual in the universe, human and non-human alike, past and future. Eventually, you come across single dark container sitting in the corner, beckoning you to come closer. You flip it over and see your own name scrawled on the bottom. This is your bottle. It was meant for you.
Search for the set-aside Bottle of Whispers weakness and add it to any investigator's hand. This card is added to their deck and does not count towards that investigator's deck size. Add this card to the victory display. Victory 1.

name: Lost Expedition
text:
If this is the the first time you read this:
Eventually, you come across the bodies of several cultists -- the missing survey team. They have abandoned their helmets and died from sudden fatal decompression. When you scan their notes, your worst fears have been confirmed. Tassilda no longer exists in this dimension, but has elevated into godhood and now resides along with her father, between the fabric of space time -- and within the core of all stars. And yet, there is a greater complication, for the survey team's notes also unmask the true nature of the King in Yellow. Our destruction gives it form, our violence gives it name, our screams give it a voice. It is no more of a deity than gravity is, no matter how many people worship and ascribe it a personality and an intelligence. It is the thermodynamic concept of Entropy itself that you face -- the gradual and inevitable decline of any system into absolute chaos. And, by all understanding of physics, there is no stopping it.
Regardless of if this is the first time you read this: Advance the current act and set this card aside, out of play.

Months have passed since you've begun your mission to save the various colonies. You've travelled between the planets and met many strange and interesting people. Some have been helpful, helping you get accustomed to the technology of the future, or pointing you towards the right direction. Most, however, have regarded you with suspicion and wariness because of the past you must unfortunately wear on your sleeves. The colonies of humanity scramble to survive the blast in any way possible.
